descriptors.emerging: I have a foundational understanding of my subject area but rely heavily on textbooks or prescribed materials. I sometimes find it challenging to explain concepts in multiple ways or connect content to real-world applications.
descriptors.developing: I demonstrate solid content knowledge and can present information clearly. I occasionally make connections between topics and real-world contexts, though interdisciplinary links are still developing.
descriptors.proficient: I demonstrate deep content knowledge and regularly connect concepts across topics and disciplines. I guide learners to think critically within the subject and design activities that reflect authentic disciplinary practice.
descriptors.transformational: I model expert disciplinary thinking, engage learners in original inquiry, and stay at the cutting edge of my field. I contribute to curriculum innovation and mentor peers in deepening their subject expertise.

descriptors.emerging: I primarily teach within my subject area and have limited experience designing lessons that draw on other disciplines. I recognise opportunities for interdisciplinary connections but rarely act on them.
descriptors.developing: I occasionally integrate concepts or skills from other disciplines into my teaching. I am aware of interdisciplinary frameworks but apply them inconsistently.
descriptors.proficient: I regularly design interdisciplinary learning experiences that help learners see the connections between subjects. I collaborate with colleagues from other departments to co-plan or co-teach.
descriptors.transformational: I lead interdisciplinary projects and professional conversations that break down siloed subject teaching. I help learners and colleagues understand how knowledge is constructed across disciplines.

descriptors.emerging: I plan lessons primarily based on curriculum requirements and personal expertise. I have limited information about individual learner needs and differentiate infrequently.
descriptors.developing: I gather some information about learner interests and readiness and attempt to vary activities. I am developing strategies for differentiation but apply them inconsistently.
descriptors.proficient: I consistently plan with learner needs, interests, and prior knowledge in mind. I differentiate content, process, and product and regularly check for understanding to adjust my teaching.
descriptors.transformational: I co-design learning with learners, empowering them to shape their own learning journey. I use learner data to innovate my planning and share effective learner-centred strategies with colleagues.

strands.name: Appropriate Methodology to the End Goal

descriptors.emerging: I primarily use one or two teaching methods regardless of the learning goal. I am building awareness of a wider range of methodologies.
descriptors.developing: I select from a small repertoire of methods and am beginning to match them to different types of learning goals. I experiment with new approaches but do not yet do this consistently.
descriptors.proficient: I deliberately select and vary teaching methods based on the intended learning outcomes. I can explain the rationale behind my methodological choices and adjust based on learner response.
descriptors.transformational: I have a rich methodological repertoire and make nuanced, evidence-informed choices. I develop and share innovative approaches and mentor others in expanding their pedagogical range.

descriptors.emerging: I am aware of diversity in my classroom but rely on whole-class approaches. I am building my understanding of how cultural background, identity, and language affect learning.
descriptors.developing: I make some adjustments for diverse learners and occasionally incorporate culturally relevant examples. I am developing a more systematic approach to inclusive design.
descriptors.proficient: I design learning experiences that are accessible and culturally responsive for all learners. I actively address barriers to participation and regularly reflect on equity in my practice.
descriptors.transformational: I lead on equity and inclusion in my school. I challenge systemic barriers, mentor colleagues, and co-create culturally responsive curriculum. Learner voice is central to how I design for equity.

descriptors.emerging: I maintain order in the classroom and ensure basic routines are in place. The physical and relational environment is functional but not yet intentionally designed to support specific types of learning.
descriptors.developing: I make deliberate choices about seating, classroom layout, and norms to support learning. I address behaviour proactively and begin to involve learners in shaping the environment.
descriptors.proficient: I design a dynamic learning environment that supports collaboration, independence, and safety. Learners understand and contribute to the norms of the space, and I adapt it to different learning purposes.
descriptors.transformational: I co-create a learning environment that learners feel ownership of. The physical, digital, and emotional dimensions are intentionally designed and continuously refined based on learner feedback.

descriptors.emerging: I use assessment tasks that are primarily prescribed by the school or curriculum. I am developing my understanding of how to design tasks that are valid, fair, and free from bias.
descriptors.developing: I design some of my own assessment tasks and consider alignment with learning goals. I am developing strategies to ensure fairness and accessibility across different learner groups.
descriptors.proficient: I design assessments that are carefully aligned to learning goals, accessible, and free from unnecessary bias. I regularly review tasks to ensure they accurately and fairly measure what learners know and can do.
descriptors.transformational: I lead assessment design within my team or school and advocate for equitable, authentic assessment approaches. I mentor colleagues in designing tasks that are rigorous, fair, and meaningful for all learners.

descriptors.emerging: I provide feedback primarily in the form of grades or brief comments. I am developing my understanding of how feedback can drive learner progress.
descriptors.developing: I provide feedback that includes some guidance on how to improve. I am building routines for formative feedback and beginning to create space for learners to act on it.
descriptors.proficient: I provide regular, specific, and actionable feedback that learners use to improve their work. I incorporate peer and self-feedback into my practice and give learners time to act on feedback before assessment.
descriptors.transformational: I have transformed the feedback culture in my classroom. Learners seek feedback proactively, use it to self-regulate, and contribute to feedback conversations. I lead professional dialogue about feedback practice.

descriptors.emerging: I collect assessment data but primarily use it for reporting. I am building my capacity to analyse patterns and use evidence to inform my teaching decisions.
descriptors.developing: I analyse some assessment data to identify areas of difficulty and adjust my planning. I am developing more systematic approaches to tracking and responding to learner progress.
descriptors.proficient: I regularly use data from a range of assessments to identify trends, adapt my teaching, and support individual learners. I communicate data-informed insights to colleagues and parents.
descriptors.transformational: I lead data-informed practice in my team or school. I design systems for collecting, analysing, and responding to learner data and mentor colleagues in using evidence to improve outcomes.

descriptors.emerging: I address academic integrity issues reactively when they arise. I have a basic understanding of school policy but do not yet systematically build integrity into my practice.
descriptors.developing: I teach and reinforce academic integrity expectations in my classroom. I am developing proactive strategies to prevent dishonesty and developing learner understanding of its importance.
descriptors.proficient: I embed academic integrity across my teaching, helping learners understand its value beyond rule-following. I design assessments that reduce the incentive to cheat and build a culture of honest scholarship.
descriptors.transformational: I lead the development or review of academic integrity policy and practice in my school. I help colleagues design integrity-embedded assessments and foster a school-wide culture of intellectual honesty.

strands.name: Responsible Use of Digital Tools for Assessment

descriptors.emerging: I use digital tools for assessment in limited ways, primarily for recording marks or basic quizzes. I am building my understanding of a wider range of digital assessment approaches.
descriptors.developing: I use digital tools to create and deliver assessments and collect learner responses. I am developing my ability to analyse digital data and select tools that are appropriate for different assessment purposes.
descriptors.proficient: I strategically select and use digital tools to design, deliver, and analyse assessments. I critically evaluate their suitability for different purposes and ensure they are used responsibly and securely.
descriptors.transformational: I lead the school's digital assessment practice, mentor colleagues in responsible tool use, and contribute to policy or system decisions about digital assessment. I actively critically evaluate emerging tools.

descriptors.emerging: I provide learners with goals and expectations but do not yet systematically develop their capacity for self-regulation. I am building my understanding of metacognitive strategies.
descriptors.developing: I introduce strategies for self-regulation and goal setting and give learners some opportunities to monitor their own progress. I am developing a more consistent approach to building these skills.
descriptors.proficient: I regularly teach and model self-regulation strategies. Learners set personal learning goals, monitor their own progress, and reflect on their approaches. I use this to inform my planning.
descriptors.transformational: I have built a classroom culture where self-regulation is central to learning. Learners take genuine ownership of their goals and development. I lead school-wide initiatives to embed metacognitive practice.

descriptors.emerging: I address digital safety and responsibility reactively. I have limited integration of digital citizenship into my teaching beyond basic rules.
descriptors.developing: I teach some aspects of digital citizenship and ethical engagement. I am developing a more integrated and proactive approach to supporting learners in navigating digital spaces responsibly.
descriptors.proficient: I consistently integrate digital citizenship into my teaching. Learners engage ethically and thoughtfully in digital spaces, and I help them develop the critical thinking needed for responsible digital participation.
descriptors.transformational: I lead the development of digital citizenship education in my school. I help learners develop sophisticated frameworks for ethical digital engagement and mentor colleagues in this area.

descriptors.emerging: I use group work occasionally but do not systematically develop collaboration skills. Group tasks are often completed individually with minimal interdependence.
descriptors.developing: I design collaborative tasks and teach some collaboration skills. Groups function with some interdependence, and I am developing strategies to make collaboration more purposeful and equitable.
descriptors.proficient: I regularly design structured collaborative tasks that develop both subject knowledge and interpersonal skills. Learners take on meaningful roles, give and receive peer feedback, and reflect on group dynamics.
descriptors.transformational: Collaborative learning is central to my classroom culture. I design sophisticated social learning experiences and build learners' capacity for productive collaboration. I lead colleagues in collaborative pedagogical design.

descriptors.emerging: I follow a prescribed curriculum and teaching approach with limited opportunities for learner choice. I am building awareness of strategies for incorporating learner voice.
descriptors.developing: I offer some choice in how learners demonstrate their learning and occasionally invite feedback on lessons. I am developing a more systematic approach to building learner agency.
descriptors.proficient: I regularly give learners meaningful choices in content, process, or product. Learner feedback informs my planning, and I create genuine space for learner voice in shaping the learning experience.
descriptors.transformational: Learner agency is a core design principle in my practice. Learners co-create curriculum, contribute to class norms, and take leadership roles. I advocate for learner voice at a school level.

descriptors.emerging: I focus primarily on the current curriculum and have limited integration of future-focused skills such as creative thinking, problem-solving, or adaptability into my lessons.
descriptors.developing: I am beginning to incorporate tasks that develop critical thinking and problem-solving. I occasionally connect learning to real-world or future contexts but do not yet do this systematically.
descriptors.proficient: I regularly design learning experiences that develop future-focused competencies: critical thinking, creativity, adaptability, and problem-solving in authentic contexts. I help learners see the relevance of their learning.
descriptors.transformational: I lead the development of future-focused curriculum and learning experiences. I connect learners to real-world challenges and help them develop the identity and skills to thrive in an uncertain future.

descriptors.emerging: I use digital tools primarily for content delivery (e.g., presentations, videos). I have limited experience designing learning experiences that integrate technology to deepen understanding.
descriptors.developing: I use a range of digital tools to support learning and am developing my ability to select tools that match specific pedagogical goals. I am building my knowledge of digital frameworks.
descriptors.proficient: I design learning experiences that strategically integrate technology to achieve specific pedagogical goals. I apply digital frameworks (e.g., SAMR, TPACK) to evaluate and improve my digital practice.
descriptors.transformational: I lead digital pedagogical design in my school. I mentor colleagues, contribute to digital strategy, and design innovative technology-enhanced learning experiences that others can learn from.

descriptors.emerging: Learners primarily consume digital content that I create or curate. I have limited experience designing tasks where learners use technology to create, collaborate, or direct their own learning.
descriptors.developing: I create some opportunities for learners to use technology to produce and share their work. I am developing strategies to use technology to increase learner choice and voice.
descriptors.proficient: I regularly design technology-enhanced tasks where learners create, collaborate, and direct their learning. Technology is a tool for learner expression and agency, not just content consumption.
descriptors.transformational: Learners in my classroom use technology with sophistication and purpose to drive their own learning. I help colleagues design for learner empowerment through technology and contribute to school digital strategy.

descriptors.emerging: I use existing digital resources in my teaching and have limited experience creating or systematically curating digital content. I am building my skills in this area.
descriptors.developing: I create some original digital content and curate resources from various online sources. I am developing a more organised approach to curation and beginning to support learners in doing the same.
descriptors.proficient: I create high-quality digital content tailored to my learners' needs and build organised digital libraries of curated resources. I teach learners to critically evaluate, create, and share digital content.
descriptors.transformational: I am a recognised creator and curator of digital content within my school or professional network. I model and teach digital content literacy and contribute to open educational resources.

descriptors.emerging: I use technology for basic assessment tasks such as online quizzes or mark recording. I am building my knowledge of digital tools that support more dynamic and formative assessment.
descriptors.developing: I use digital tools for formative assessment and am developing my ability to analyse and respond to digital data. I give some feedback through digital channels.
descriptors.proficient: I use a range of digital tools to design, deliver, and analyse assessments. I provide timely, actionable digital feedback and teach learners to use digital tools to track their own progress.
descriptors.transformational: I lead digital assessment practice in my school. I design and evaluate digital feedback systems, mentor colleagues, and contribute to the school's approach to data-informed digital assessment.

strands.name: AI Literacy and Ethical Use of EdTech

descriptors.emerging: I am aware of AI tools but have limited experience using or teaching with them. I am beginning to develop my understanding of the ethical implications of AI in education.
descriptors.developing: I use some AI tools in my practice and am developing a framework for evaluating their educational value. I occasionally address AI literacy with learners but do not yet do this systematically.
descriptors.proficient: I use AI tools critically and purposefully in my teaching and design learning experiences that develop learners' AI literacy. I help learners engage with AI tools ethically and with understanding.
descriptors.transformational: I lead AI literacy education in my school. I contribute to policy on AI use, mentor colleagues in ethical AI integration, and help learners develop sophisticated frameworks for understanding AI's role in society.

strands.name: Professional Learning and Networking through Collaboration

descriptors.emerging: I attend required professional development but do not yet seek out additional learning opportunities. My professional network is limited, and I rarely engage in collaborative professional learning.
descriptors.developing: I participate in professional learning communities and occasionally share practice with colleagues. I am building my professional network and beginning to take ownership of my professional development.
descriptors.proficient: I proactively seek out professional learning opportunities and contribute actively to collaborative communities of practice. I regularly share and receive feedback on my practice from a wide professional network.
descriptors.transformational: I lead professional learning in my school or beyond. I design and facilitate professional development, contribute to research or networks, and help build a culture of continuous professional growth.

descriptors.emerging: I reflect on my teaching informally and occasionally make adjustments based on how lessons go. Reflection is not yet a structured or regular part of my practice.
descriptors.developing: I engage in structured reflection after lessons or units and use this to inform my next steps. I am developing more systematic approaches to reflective practice.
descriptors.proficient: Reflection is a regular and structured part of my practice. I use a range of tools (journals, video, peer observation) to analyse my teaching and make evidence-informed changes.
descriptors.transformational: I model and lead reflective practice in my school. I mentor colleagues in developing their reflective capacity, contribute to school improvement processes, and connect my reflection to broader professional dialogue.

descriptors.emerging: I am aware of educational research but do not yet systematically engage with it or conduct my own classroom inquiry. I am building my understanding of action research approaches.
descriptors.developing: I engage with educational research and occasionally conduct small-scale inquiry into my own practice. I am developing the skills and confidence to conduct and share practitioner research.
descriptors.proficient: I regularly conduct classroom-based research and use findings to improve my practice and share insights with colleagues. I engage critically with educational literature to inform my inquiry.
descriptors.transformational: I lead practitioner research initiatives in my school and contribute to the wider educational research community. I mentor colleagues in research design and disseminate findings through publications or presentations.

descriptors.emerging: I use curriculum guidelines and past experience as the primary basis for planning. I make limited use of data to adapt my practice and have a basic understanding of how data can inform planning.
descriptors.developing: I use some learner data to inform my planning and am developing more systematic approaches. I am building my capacity to identify patterns and respond adaptively.
descriptors.proficient: I use a range of data sources (assessments, observations, learner feedback) to plan adaptively. I monitor the impact of my teaching decisions and adjust my approaches in response to evidence.
descriptors.transformational: I lead data-driven planning processes in my team or school. I design data collection systems, mentor colleagues in using evidence to improve practice, and contribute to school-wide adaptive planning.

descriptors.emerging: I manage my professional responsibilities but find it difficult to maintain a sustainable work-life balance. I am building my awareness of wellbeing strategies and have limited support structures in place.
descriptors.developing: I am developing strategies for managing my workload and maintaining my wellbeing. I occasionally seek support from colleagues or mentors and am building more sustainable professional habits.
descriptors.proficient: I proactively manage my workbad and wellbeing and have established sustainable professional routines. I seek and offer peer support, set boundaries, and model healthy professional practices.
descriptors.transformational: I lead wellbeing initiatives in my school and advocate for systemic conditions that support teacher sustainability. I mentor colleagues in developing sustainable practice and contribute to school culture around wellbeing.
